notes: Hard crypto-breach-recovery pipeline bundling four competencies that must ALL hold. (1) C-d9425275 easy/medium floor: the recovered username+password must land as /app/creds.txt with exact schema. (2) C-38bb2e3e hard: a deleted private key + certificate must be carved byte-exactly out of a length-prefixed (LVPR/LVCR) carrier into a clean dir that contains nothing else; the verifier re-runs the carve on a different carrier and byte-compares. (3) C-cf32bd95 hard: the agent must read /app/src/check.c, invert the bijective per-byte transform f(x)=((x*0x35+0x2f)^0xa5)&0xff (mod-256 inverse lookup) to turn the stored passhash fingerprint into a valid 12-byte printable secret; the verifier recompiles check.c and runs it on the recovered secret. (4) C-ce46ee62 medium: single-byte-key WAL recovery - find k by XOR-matching the native magic 37 7f 06 82, decode, restore ledge.db-wal, and read the un-checkpointed cfg rows. Difficulty is hard because three claimed competencies carry hard floors and the dependent_stages chain (decode wal -> read DB -> invert check -> carve -> concat key.pem -> write creds) means any single wrong byte/magic/path breaks the whole effort; quantitative_correctness matters for the byte-exact magic, byte-exact carve, and byte-exact key.pem concatenation; hidden cases re-run decode.bin unwal on a different-key WAL and carve on a different carrier (generalization). No unsafe actions demanded, no interaction statefulness.
